16	id: https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset
17	name: CHoRUS Dataset
18	title: "Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI"
19	description: >-
20	  The CHoRUS dataset is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access dataset of
21	  acute and critical care hospital admissions, assembled retrospectively by the CHoRUS Network, one
22	  of four data generation projects in the NIH Common Fund's Bridge2AI program. Data are contributed
23	  by 14 data acquisition hospitals among the 20 academic centers in the collaboration, whose
24	  membership is given as more than 60 consortium members. Structured electronic health record data
25	  are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model; unstructured EHR text is extracted and tokenized
26	  with the OHNLP toolkit; imaging is drawn from hospital PACS in DICOM; telemetry waveforms from
27	  bedside monitors and gateway/middleware are released in WFDB; and EEG waveforms from hospital EEG
28	  databases are released in EDF+ and Persyst formats. Social determinants of health and contextual
29	  factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital are also acquired. The project website
30	  reports a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU, and NICU settings,
31	  1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform
32	  data, against an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions covering 9 data
33	  modalities from 14 contributing hospitals. The nine documented data types are demographics,
34	  medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses, clinical notes, imaging,
35	  waveform telemetry, and EEG waveform; every one of them is under controlled access. OMOP and
36	  telemetry data sit in a cloud enclave, clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites
37	  with only tokens centralized, and as of August 2025 imaging de-identification for a larger cohort
38	  and EEG extraction were still in process. The project also sequesters a holdout test set for
39	  external validation of models.

71	  The project website carries a site-wide banner reading "This repoitory is under review for
72	  potential modification in compliance with Administration directives." The misspelling of
73	  "repository" is reproduced as published. The same website carries the funding statement "This
74	  project is funded by the NIH under award number OT2OD032701. The content on this website is solely

77	source_caveats: >-
78	  The two sources that quantify the dataset disagree. The tier-2 project documentation
79	  (chorus4ai.org) states a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions and 7,642
80	  admissions with radiology data; the tier-4 cohort_2_webinar states that "As of August 2025, covers
81	  14 different hospitals with over 45K unique admissions" and that 1000 images are currently
82	  available. The tier-2 values are stated in this record, with the webinar's August 2025 snapshot
83	  reported where it describes modality readiness; the conflict is also recorded on the individual
84	  values it affects. The two imaging figures are expressed in different units (images versus
85	  admissions with radiology data) and may not be directly comparable. A single OTHER term in
86	  conforms_to_standard stands for three distinct standards the registered enum does not cover: EDF+,
87	  Persyst, and the OHNLP open source schema. The WFDB entry likewise covers a schema the source
88	  describes as extended rather than plain WFDB. The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version
89	  identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset, and does not state the language of the
90	  dataset content.

336	- bias_type: representation_bias
337	  bias_description: >-
338	    The project treats cohort balance and diversity as an open risk to be managed: patient-focused
339	    efforts determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting
340	    for social determinants of health, and the stated goal is the most diverse AI-ready data set for
341	    improving recovery from acute illness.
342	  mitigation_strategy: >-
343	    Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort, and
344	    sampling at scale is designed to capture comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical
345	    treatment strategies.

347	known_limitations:
348	- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
349	  limitation_description: >-
350	    Modality availability is uneven and still developing. As of August 2025 the cohort 2 webinar
351	    reported that 1000 images were available with de-identification in process for a larger imaging
352	    cohort, that EEG extraction was still in process, and that published metadata was only planned
353	    rather than available for clinical notes, imaging, and EEG. The project website separately
354	    reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data in the current released dataset.
355	  recommended_mitigation: >-
356	    Confirm current modality availability with the CHoRUS data access contacts before planning
357	    analyses that depend on imaging, EEG, or note tokens.
358	- limitation_type: scope_limitation

360	    The released dataset is a partial build: 50,000 patient admissions against an anticipated final
361	    dataset of 100,000 patient admissions.
362	- limitation_type: integration_limitation

364	    Clinical notes are not centralized with the rest of the data; they are stored locally at
365	    contributing sites and only tokens produced by the OHNLP toolkit are available in the enclave,
366	    which constrains analyses requiring raw narrative text.
367	- limitation_type: representativeness_limitation
368	  limitation_description: >-
369	    Data are contributed by 14 hospitals drawn from the 20 academic centers in the collaboration, so
370	    the cohort reflects the case mix and practice patterns of those participating academic centers.

id: https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset
name: CHoRUS Dataset
title: "Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI"
description: >-
  The CHoRUS dataset is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access dataset of
  acute and critical care hospital admissions, assembled retrospectively by the CHoRUS Network, one
  of four data generation projects in the NIH Common Fund's Bridge2AI program. Data are contributed
  by 14 data acquisition hospitals among the 20 academic centers in the collaboration, whose
  membership is given as more than 60 consortium members. Structured electronic health record data
  are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model; unstructured EHR text is extracted and tokenized
  with the OHNLP toolkit; imaging is drawn from hospital PACS in DICOM; telemetry waveforms from
  bedside monitors and gateway/middleware are released in WFDB; and EEG waveforms from hospital EEG
  databases are released in EDF+ and Persyst formats. Social determinants of health and contextual
  factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital are also acquired. The project website
  reports a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU, and NICU settings,
  1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform
  data, against an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions covering 9 data
  modalities from 14 contributing hospitals. The nine documented data types are demographics,
  medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses, clinical notes, imaging,
  waveform telemetry, and EEG waveform; every one of them is under controlled access. OMOP and
  telemetry data sit in a cloud enclave, clinical notes remain stored locally at contributing sites
  with only tokens centralized, and as of August 2025 imaging de-identification for a larger cohort
  and EEG extraction were still in process. The project also sequesters a holdout test set for
  external validation of models.
status: partially released
page: https://chorus4ai.org/
created_by: CHoRUS Consortium

conforms_to: >-
  Structured EHR data conform to the OMOP Common Data Model (with extensions for nursing flowsheets);
  imaging conforms to DICOM; waveform telemetry conforms to WFDB, described in the source as a
  PhysioNet schema extended; EEG conforms to EDF+ and Persyst; tokenized clinical notes conform to
  the OHNLP open source schema.
conforms_to_standard:
- OMOP_CDM
- DICOM
- WFDB
- OTHER
conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema

notes: >-
  The project website carries a site-wide banner reading "This repoitory is under review for
  potential modification in compliance with Administration directives." The misspelling of
  "repository" is reproduced as published. The same website carries the funding statement "This
  project is funded by the NIH under award number OT2OD032701. The content on this website is solely
  the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the
  NIH."
source_caveats: >-
  The two sources that quantify the dataset disagree. The tier-2 project documentation
  (chorus4ai.org) states a current released dataset of 50,000 patient admissions and 7,642
  admissions with radiology data; the tier-4 cohort_2_webinar states that "As of August 2025, covers
  14 different hospitals with over 45K unique admissions" and that 1000 images are currently
  available. The tier-2 values are stated in this record, with the webinar's August 2025 snapshot
  reported where it describes modality readiness; the conflict is also recorded on the individual
  values it affects. The two imaging figures are expressed in different units (images versus
  admissions with radiology data) and may not be directly comparable. A single OTHER term in
  conforms_to_standard stands for three distinct standards the registered enum does not cover: EDF+,
  Persyst, and the OHNLP open source schema. The WFDB entry likewise covers a schema the source
  describes as extended rather than plain WFDB. The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version
  identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset, and does not state the language of the
  dataset content.

purposes:
- response: >-
    Meet the need of generating data for ML/AI applications aimed at characterizing acute and
    critical care illness, predicting complications, and measuring treatment response among patients
    with acute or critical illness.
- response: >-
    Develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring the methods promote
    privacy, accountability, and clinical benefit, and while promoting a new generation of AI
    clinicians and scientists.
- response: >-
    Develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set to answer the
    grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.
- response: >-
    Create ethically sourced datasets and tools around artificial intelligence and create best
    practices for AI in health, as one of four data generation projects in the NIH Bridge2AI
    consortium.

addressing_gaps:
- response: >-
    There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine
    learning in critical care; developing high-resolution multi-center data sets is a critical first
    step towards actionable and trustworthy AI.
- response: >-
    Existing critical care data lack the diversity and resolution needed for AI; the project acquires
    and standardizes a dataset of unprecedented diversity and high resolution across a multi-center
    network.
- response: >-
    Multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging, and text data are not harmonized; unified standards and
    validated semantic mappings are developed to make them interoperable.

- use_category: External validation of AI models
  usage_notes: >-
    A holdout test set is provisioned specifically for external validation of models developed
    elsewhere.
- use_category: Training and workforce development in clinical AI
  usage_notes: >-
    The dataset is used within the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud for
    hands-on AI/ML coursework, canonical Jupyter Notebooks, and OHDSI/OMOP instruction, including
    trainee development of use cases and works-in-progress posters, conference abstracts, and

acquisition_methods:
- was_directly_observed: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    Retrospective extraction of structured electronic health record data (demographics, medication
    administration with dosing time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration,
    procedures documented by providers, high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation, and
    provider-documented diagnoses) from contributing hospital systems, standardized to the OMOP
    Common Data Model.
- was_directly_observed: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    Waveform telemetry captured from bedside monitors through hospital gateway/middleware and
    delivered in WFDB format.
- was_directly_observed: true
  acquisition_details: Imaging studies retrieved from hospital PACS in DICOM format.
- was_directly_observed: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    EEG waveforms extracted from hospital EEG databases in EDF+ and Persyst formats; extraction was
    still in process as of August 2025.
- was_directly_observed: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    Clinical notes documented by providers are extracted from hospital systems and tokenized using
    the OHNLP toolkit; the notes themselves are stored locally at contributing sites and only tokens
    are centralized.

collection_mechanisms:
- mechanism_details: >-
    Bedside physiologic monitors together with hospital gateway/middleware supply waveform telemetry.
- mechanism_details: Hospital picture archiving and communication systems (PACS) supply imaging.
- mechanism_details: Hospital EEG databases supply EEG waveform recordings.
- mechanism_details: >-
    The OHNLP toolkit is used to extract and tokenize unstructured clinical notes.
- mechanism_details: >-
    The chorus-extract-upload Python tool in the chorus-ai GitHub organization provides tools to

data_collectors:
- collector_details: >-
    Fourteen of the twenty academic centers in the CHoRUS collaboration contribute as Data
    Acquisition centers, extracting and delivering clinical data extracts to the project.
- collector_details: >-
    Data site managers at contributing sites follow an interactive workflow and step-by-step standard
    operating procedures published in the Chorus_SOP repository, which have undergone an internal
    validation and review process, and report progress through GitHub or a Google Form that updates
    the Standards Project and Data Acquisition Project boards.

    Data collection is retrospective: clinical data are extracted from hospital clinical systems

collection_timeframes:
- timeframe_details: >-
    Data collection is described as retrospective and is carried out over the NIH award period, which

known_biases:
- bias_type: representation_bias
  bias_description: >-
    The project treats cohort balance and diversity as an open risk to be managed: patient-focused
    efforts determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting
    for social determinants of health, and the stated goal is the most diverse AI-ready data set for
    improving recovery from acute illness.
  mitigation_strategy: >-
    Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort, and
    sampling at scale is designed to capture comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical
    treatment strategies.

known_limitations:
- limitation_type: coverage_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Modality availability is uneven and still developing. As of August 2025 the cohort 2 webinar
    reported that 1000 images were available with de-identification in process for a larger imaging
    cohort, that EEG extraction was still in process, and that published metadata was only planned
    rather than available for clinical notes, imaging, and EEG. The project website separately
    reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data in the current released dataset.
  recommended_mitigation: >-
    Confirm current modality availability with the CHoRUS data access contacts before planning
    analyses that depend on imaging, EEG, or note tokens.
- limitation_type: scope_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    The released dataset is a partial build: 50,000 patient admissions against an anticipated final
    dataset of 100,000 patient admissions.
- limitation_type: integration_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Clinical notes are not centralized with the rest of the data; they are stored locally at
    contributing sites and only tokens produced by the OHNLP toolkit are available in the enclave,
    which constrains analyses requiring raw narrative text.
- limitation_type: representativeness_limitation
  limitation_description: >-
    Data are contributed by 14 hospitals drawn from the 20 academic centers in the collaboration, so
    the cohort reflects the case mix and practice patterns of those participating academic centers.

preprocessing_strategies:
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Source clinical data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, with schema extensions used
    for high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Unstructured electronic health record text is extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit and
    represented in the OHNLP open source schema.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification before release.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Waveforms are prepared and converted using the waveform conversion scripts and documentation in
    the chorus_waveform and chorus_waveform_resources repositories, with telemetry released in WFDB
    (described as a PhysioNet schema extended) and EEG in EDF+ and Persyst.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    OMOP Location entities are geocoded via DeGauss using the open source UF-Geocoding code, a fork
    of bihorac-LAB/Exposome maintained in the chorus-ai GitHub organization.

cleaning_strategies:

    Characterization reports are produced and returned to sites following their data submissions,
    using the CHoRUSReports repository, so that contributing sites can identify and resolve issues in
    their extracts.
- cleaning_details: >-
    Semantic mappings from source formats to international standards are validated; clinical
    collaborators contribute to pooled tabular mappings in the chorus-mapping repository under an
    associated clinical validation standard operating procedure.

labeling_strategies:
- labeling_details: >-
    A visualization and annotation environment is developed to label data with targets important for
    prediction, as part of the project's capability to acquire, standardize, tokenize, store,
    visualize, and label data across the multi-center network.

70	    """Back-compatible wrapper: superseded records are not valid."""

198	    print("=" * 60)
199	    print("SUMMARY (judged against a schema):")
200	    for where in ("live", "kept"):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Validate D4D evaluation JSON files against their schemas.

This ensures evaluations conform to the standardized schema, which in turn
ensures HTML renderers can reliably parse the output.
"""
import argparse
import json
import re as _re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

try:
    import jsonschema
    from jsonschema import validate, ValidationError
except ImportError:
    print("ERROR: jsonschema package not installed")
    print("Install with: pip install jsonschema")
    sys.exit(1)


def load_schema(schema_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Load JSON Schema file."""
    with open(schema_path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)


def load_evaluation(eval_path: Path) -> Dict:
    """Load evaluation JSON file."""
    with open(eval_path, 'r') as f:
        return json.load(f)


#: Top-level keys of the shape that preceded the current agent contract.
#: rubric10 evaluations recorded before 2026 report `summary_scores` and
#: `element_scores`; the agents have instructed `overall_score` and `elements`
#: since. Such a record is not wrong, it is a different vintage — reporting it
#: as invalid buries the records that really are.
SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS = ("summary_scores", "element_scores")


def classify(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[str, List[str]]:
    """Validate, distinguishing a superseded shape from a wrong value.

    Returns `("valid" | "superseded" | "invalid", errors)`.

    The distinction is the point. All 28 recorded evaluations failed before the
    schemas were brought up to the agents (#323), and "Invalid: 28" said nothing
    about which were merely old. Of the 20 that still fail, 12 predate the
    contract and 8 report `max_points: 84` — a maximum the rubric has never had
    (#314). Only the second kind is a defect in a record.
    """
    errors = []
    try:
        validate(instance=eval_data, schema=schema)
        return "valid", []
    except ValidationError as e:
        errors.append(f"Validation error: {e.message}")
        errors.append(f"  Path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.path)}")
        if e.schema_path:
            errors.append(f"  Schema path: {' -> '.join(str(p) for p in e.schema_path)}")
        if any(k in eval_data for k in SUPERSEDED_SHAPE_KEYS):
            return "superseded", errors
        return "invalid", errors


def validate_evaluation(eval_data: Dict, schema: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, List[str]]:
    """Back-compatible wrapper: superseded records are not valid."""
    status, errors = classify(eval_data, schema)
    return status == "valid", errors


def validate_outputs(paths: List[Path], rubric: str | None = None,
                     schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
    """Require each explicitly named new output to pass its semantic schema.

    Directory names and superseded shapes do not exempt a new output. This
    path reads only the files named by the caller, so an evaluator can check
    its own output without reading another evaluator's judgements (#833).
    """
    schema_dir = schema_dir or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src/download/prompts"
    names = {"rubric10-semantic": "rubric10_semantic_schema.json",
             "rubric20-semantic": "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"}
    failed = not paths
    for path in paths:
        try:
            doc = load_evaluation(path)
            if not isinstance(doc, dict):
                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
            declared = doc.get("rubric")
            if not isinstance(declared, str) or declared not in names:
                raise ValueError(f"no semantic evaluation schema for rubric {declared!r}")
            if rubric is not None and declared != rubric:
                raise ValueError(f"expected {rubric}, found {declared}")
            valid, errors = validate_evaluation(doc, load_schema(schema_dir / names[declared]))
            if not valid:
                raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
        except (OSError, ValueError, jsonschema.SchemaError) as exc:
            print(f"INVALID {path}: {exc}")
            failed = True
        else:
            print(f"VALID {path}: {declared}")
    return int(failed)


#: A directory whose name marks its contents as kept evidence rather than a
#: live artifact: an archive, a superseded set, or a dated snapshot of one
#: arm's scores. An invalid record in one of these is what an older
#: instrument produced and must not be rewritten to satisfy today's schema,
#: so it is reported and does not fail the run.
KEPT_DIR = _re.compile(r"^(?:_archive|superseded)|^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(?:[_-]|$)")


def is_kept(path: Path, base: Path) -> bool:
    """Is any directory between `base` and `path` an archive marker?"""
    return any(KEPT_DIR.match(part) for part in path.relative_to(base).parts[:-1])


def discover(base: Path) -> List[Path]:
    """Every evaluation JSON under `base`, at any depth.

    The loop was `{rubric}_semantic/concatenated/*.json` — one directory per
    rubric, one level deep (#833). That reached 28 of the 204 semantic
    artifacts on disk: not `label_aware/`, which is where every evaluation
    since 2026-08 lives and which the cross-arm table reads, not the dated
    per-arm subdirectories beside it, and not the archives. The rubric a file
    declares decides which schema it is judged against, so the directory does
    not have to.
    """
    return sorted(base.rglob("*_evaluation.json"))


def main(eval_base: Path | None = None, schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> int:
    """Validate every evaluation JSON under `data/evaluation_llm`.

    The two roots are arguments so that the exit code — the thing #833 asked
    for, and the thing four tests of the helpers did not reach — can be
    exercised end to end over a tree built for the purpose.
    """
    base_dir = Path(__file__).parent.parent
    schema_dir = schema_dir or base_dir / "src" / "download" / "prompts"
    eval_base = eval_base or base_dir / "data" / "evaluation_llm"

    schemas = {
        "rubric10-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric10_semantic_schema.json"),
        "rubric20-semantic": load_schema(schema_dir / "rubric20_semantic_schema.json"),
    }

    eval_files = discover(eval_base)
    if not eval_files:
        print(f"No evaluation files found in {eval_base}")
        return 1

    print(f"Found {len(eval_files)} evaluation file(s) under {eval_base}\n")

    counts = {("live", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
    counts.update({("kept", k): 0 for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")})
    no_schema: Dict[str, int] = {}
    live_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []
    kept_invalid: List[Tuple[Path, List[str]]] = []

    for eval_file in eval_files:
        where = "kept" if is_kept(eval_file, eval_base) else "live"
        shown = eval_file.relative_to(eval_base)
        try:
            eval_data = load_evaluation(eval_file)
            if not isinstance(eval_data, dict):
                raise ValueError("evaluation must be a JSON object")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"❌ {shown}: failed to load: {e}")
            counts[(where, "unreadable")] += 1
            continue

        rubric = eval_data.get("rubric", "unknown")
        if rubric not in schemas:
            # Named and counted, not skipped in silence: the presence-style
            # rubric10/rubric20 outputs have no schema in this repository, and
            # a reader of the summary should see that they were not judged.
            no_schema[str(rubric)] = no_schema.get(str(rubric), 0) + 1
            continue

        status, errors = classify(eval_data, schemas[rubric])
        counts[(where, status)] += 1
        if status == "invalid":
            (kept_invalid if where == "kept" else live_invalid).append((shown, errors))
        elif status == "superseded":
            print(f"🕐 {shown}: superseded shape — {errors[0]}")

    for label, rows in (("live", live_invalid), ("kept as evidence", kept_invalid)):
        for shown, errors in rows:
            print(f"❌ {shown} ({label}):")
            for error in errors:
                print(f"     {error}")

    print()
    print("=" * 60)
    print("SUMMARY (judged against a schema):")
    for where in ("live", "kept"):
        row = {k: counts[(where, k)] for k in ("valid", "superseded", "invalid", "unreadable")}
        print(f"  {where:5}  valid {row['valid']:4}  superseded {row['superseded']:3}  "
              f"invalid {row['invalid']:3}  unreadable {row['unreadable']:3}")
    if no_schema:
        print("  no schema in this repository, not judged: "
              + ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(no_schema.items())))
    print("=" * 60)

    # A superseded record is historical output of a contract that no longer
    # applies, and one kept under an archive marker is evidence of what an
    # older instrument produced: reported, never rewritten to pass. Only a
    # live invalid artifact fails the run.
    return 0 if not live_invalid and not counts[("live", "unreadable")] else 1


def cli(argv: List[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--file", type=Path, action="append", dest="files",
                        help="validate this exact new output strictly; repeat for multiple files")
    parser.add_argument("--rubric", choices=("rubric10-semantic", "rubric20-semantic"),
                        help="require the named outputs to use this rubric")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.rubric and not args.files:
        parser.error("--rubric requires --file")
    return validate_outputs(args.files, args.rubric) if args.files else main()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(cli())
